items.bold: TRUMP extended ceasefire to Wednesday evening — 2 more days (CNN/Bloomberg confirmed).
items.text: Trump told Bloomberg in phone interview Monday: ceasefire now ends "Wednesday evening Washington time" — he had previously said it was a two-week ceasefire expiring Tuesday. military.t: Nuclear Gap: US 20yr vs Iran 5yr. Assets Gap: Iran $20B+ vs US Much Less. Three Unresolved.
military.d: Three core issues remain unresolved: (1) Nuclear enrichment duration — US wanted 20-year pause, Iran offered 5 years; (2) Frozen assets — Iran demands $20B+, US offering much less; (3) Hormuz — Iran wants sovereignty recognition and toll rights, US wants unconditional free navigation. Vance will propose what can be proposed. Iran's public face says no, private signals say maybe. Wednesday is the deadline. After Wednesday: either a deal, or the most destructive phase of this war begins.

DAY 52 PRE-MARKET. USS Spruance seized Touska (CENTCOM video confirmed). Iran OFFICIALLY rejected second round talks (IRNA) — excessive demands, blockade violation. IRGC Aerospace commander: rebuilding missiles and drones faster than before war. ZERO tankers crossed Hormuz Sunday. Brent $95.64 (+5.8%) Sunday open. Ceasefire expires TOMORROW Apr 22. India markets open 9:15 AM IST — most dangerous session since Feb 28. Sensex gap-down risk: 70,000-73,000 if ceasefire lapses.

DAY 52. USS SPRUANCE SEIZED IRANIAN CARGO SHIP TOUSKA — fired into engine room, Marines boarded. Iran vowed swift response: "Armed forces will soon respond." ZERO tankers crossed Hormuz Sunday (CNN). Brent +5.8% to $95.64. Vance+Witkoff+Kushner heading Islamabad Monday — Iran NOT confirmed, IRNA says declined. Trump: knock out every power plant and bridge. Ceasefire expires Wed Apr 22. IMO: 24 incidents total. Two more Indian-flag vessels attacked Apr 18. Brent $95+. India Monday open: extreme volatility.

HORMUZ CLOSED. IRGC targeting all vessels. No Indian tanker confirmed crossing Apr 19. Indian VLCC (2M bbl) fired on Apr 18, turned back. MEA urged Iran to resume. US officials travelling to Pakistan. Nuclear progress before crisis. Brent ~$96-97. Ceasefire Apr 22 — 3 days.

assessment.headline: DAY 52, 10 PM MON: CEASEFIRE EXTENDED TO WEDNESDAY. Iran publicly refusing talks — but privately ambiguous. Islamabad on lockdown. Sensex +27 (flat), VIX +19. Brent $95-96. Wednesday = ceasefire expiry + Infosys. 48 hours to deal or war.
assessment.body:
Day 52 closes with the war's clock moved to Wednesday.

THE WEDNESDAY DEADLINE — TWO MORE DAYS
• Trump told Bloomberg: ceasefire now ends "Wednesday evening Washington time"
• Originally slated for Tuesday — gave 2 extra days
• "Highly unlikely I'd extend it" further if no deal
• "If there's no deal, I would certainly expect" fighting to resume
• Wednesday evening ET = Wednesday night IST ~9-11 PM IST

THE IRAN PARADOX — PUBLICLY NO, PRIVATELY MAYBE
• Official position: Baghaei: "no plans" to travel to Pakistan — US "not serious"
• Iran FM to Pakistan: US actions are "bad intentions and lack of seriousness"
• BusinessToday: Iran called US demands "childish"
• BUT: Iranian sources told CNN delegation expected in Pakistan Tuesday
• BUT: Al Jazeera by late Monday — "unclear whether Vance travels"
• Strategy: Witkoff+Kushner go first, Vance joins if Iran actually shows
• This is classic Iran negotiating: public refusal + private preparation

ISLAMABAD IS PHYSICALLY READY
• 10,000 extra security forces deployed
• Serena Hotel (first round venue) under security lockdown
• US Air Force C-17 landed at Nur Khan airbase (AFP photo confirmed)
• At least four US government aircraft carrying communications equipment
• Infrastructure is in place for talks to begin if Iran reverses

MARKETS — NERVOUS BUT HOLDING
• Sensex 78,520 (+27 / flat). Nifty 24,365 (+11)
• India VIX +10.5% to 19.01 — fear gauge clearly elevated
• Brent $95-96 — moderated from $95.22 open after ceasefire extension
• No panic, but no confidence either
• Wednesday is the next major inflection point

INDIA WEDNESDAY RISK — DOUBLE EVENT
• Ceasefire expiry outcome (most important)
• Infosys Q4 results (domestic IT bellwether)
• Both on the same day
• Rupee ~94.00-94.50 — under pressure but not panicking

THE 48-HOUR DECISION TREE
• If Iran attends talks Tuesday and framework agreed by Wednesday: Brent falls to $80-88, Sensex 80,000-83,000, India VIX back to 13-14
• If Iran refuses, ceasefire lapses Wednesday: Brent $110-120, Sensex 72,000-75,000, rupee tests 97-100
• If de-facto extension (both sides hold fire but no deal): Brent $92-96, Sensex 76,000-78,500

VERDICT: The war clock now reads 48 hours. Iran publicly says no but privately may be preparing to attend. Islamabad is physically ready. Vance is standing by. The question is whether Iran arrives at the Serena Hotel on Tuesday. If they do, the world gets a deal framework before Wednesday evening. If they don't, the most destructive phase of this war begins on Thursday morning.
